title: Perfectly consistent 4x4 matrix (CR exactly 0)
description: A 4x4 matrix constructed as a_ij = w_i / w_j from the weight vector w = (8/15, 4/15, 2/15, 1/15). Because the matrix is perfectly consistent, any correct implementation must return CR = 0 (to numerical precision), lambda_max = n, and the construction weights exactly; eigenvector and approximate prioritization methods coincide on consistent matrices.

source.citation: Constructed for this fixture set; see provenance fields.

scale.name: saaty-1-9
scale.notes: Judgments on Saaty's fundamental 1-9 scale; reciprocals (e.g. 1/3) and intermediate or fractional values are valid entries. Matrix entries may be given as numbers or as fraction strings such as "1/3".

ri_table.name: saaty
ri_table.source: T. L. Saaty, The Analytic Hierarchy Process, McGraw-Hill, 1980. Values as tabulated in J. A. Alonso and M. T. Lamata, 'Consistency in the analytic hierarchy process: a new approach', International Journal of Uncertainty, Fuzziness and Knowledge-Based Systems 14(4), 2006, Table 1 (Wharton column).

provenance.method: Constructed from a weight vector w by setting a_ij = w_i / w_j, which makes the matrix perfectly consistent by construction: the principal eigenvector equals w exactly, lambda_max = n exactly, and CI = CR = 0 exactly (not merely approximately).
